_about.table: Wi-Fi adapters by PCI id (vvvv:dddd, lower-case hex), then a fallback by vendor id
_about.fields: Name (shown to the person), Driver (the in-tree kernel module, or proprietary or none), MinKernel (the earliest kernel with usable support; empty means long supported), Status (ok, warn or fail), Note (one line, shown verbatim), Source (how we know: a kernel commit, release notes, a machine capture in evaluate/windows/corpus; empty means nobody has cited one yet), Verified (the date the Source was last checked, or empty)
_about.rule: Adding a device is one entry and a cited source. 'It should work' is not a source.

10ec:8821.Name: Realtek RTL8821CE
10ec:8821.Note: Known for unstable throughput and suspend/resume drops on some models.

10ec:c821.Name: Realtek RTL8821CE
10ec:c821.Note: Known for unstable throughput and suspend/resume drops on some models.

14c3:7925.Name: MediaTek MT7925
14c3:7925.Note: Wi-Fi 7 card, supported from kernel 6.7. On older kernels there is no driver at all - you will boot with no wireless.
14c3:7925.Source: the G16 (the development machine, MediaTek MT7925)

14e4:4365.Name: Broadcom BCM43142
14e4:4365.Note: Broadcom. Poorly supported even with the out-of-tree driver. Replacing the M.2 card with an Intel AX200 (~$20) is the standard fix.

14e4:43a3.Name: Broadcom BCM4350
14e4:43a3.Note: Broadcom. No working in-tree driver. Needs the out-of-tree wl module, which must be compiled - and you cannot download it without a network connection you do not yet have. Bring a USB Ethernet adapter or a phone for USB tethering.

14e4:43b1.Name: Broadcom BCM4352
14e4:43b1.Note: Broadcom. Same chicken-and-egg problem: the driver needs a network connection to install. Bring USB Ethernet or a tethered phone.

17cb:1101.Name: Qualcomm QCA6390
17cb:1101.Note: Firmware is fussy; Bluetooth coexistence bugs are common. Usually works, occasionally does not.

17cb:1103.Name: Qualcomm WCN6855
17cb:1103.Note: Needs vendor firmware blobs that some distros ship late.

8086:272b.Name: Intel BE200
8086:272b.Note: Wi-Fi 7 card. Needs a recent kernel; some vendors ship it on boards that only whitelist it under Windows.

10ec.Note: Unrecognised Realtek card. Support ranges from fine to flaky depending on the exact part.

14c3.Note: Unrecognised MediaTek card. Recent MediaTek parts are supported but often only on very new kernels - prefer a current-release distro.

14e4.Note: Unrecognised Broadcom card. Broadcom wireless is the single most common cause of "no internet after installing Linux". Bring USB Ethernet or a tethered phone.

168c.Note: Unrecognised Atheros card. This family is generally well supported.

17cb.Note: Unrecognised Qualcomm card. Newer ath12k parts need very recent kernels and firmware.

8086.Note: Unrecognised Intel card. Intel wireless is in-tree and near-universally supported; very likely fine.
